title: Generic stateful I/O wave 2 baseline
goal: Establish the fail-closed capture, classification, matrix, documentation, and validation baseline for generic stateful I/O resource graph wave 2 before graduating new support. The baseline must distinguish append/non-append writable file descriptors, Unix socket shapes, eventfd/epoll/anon-inode resources, runtime file-lock evidence, mmap state, and inotify/fanotify state, while refusing all newly observed unsupported classes before target loader launch with exact evidence and no target pid. No new support class is graduated in this goal.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove writable regular-file descriptors are captured and classified into append-only candidates versus non-append writable ambiguity, with both classes refused in this baseline unless already covered by an existing bespoke envelope.
proofChecklist.evidence: Writable regular-file descriptor classes are now distinct and refused. Focused tests prove append-only fd candidates produce access=append-only-refused, cursor policy append-only-end, and refusalClass appendOnlyRegularFileCursor, while non-append writable fds remain writableRegularFileCursor. proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented parsed UNIX_FD preflight evidence from /proc/net/unix and exact fail-closed Unix socket subtype classification. currentEvidence.summary: Inspected current generic resource graph baseline before implementation. Current coverage already refuses non-read-only regular files as writableRegularFileCursor, deleted files as regularFileDeleted, broad sockets as socket unless they are idle loopback TCP listeners, broad unknown anon_inode resources as unknown, inotify-like unknown paths as inotify, file locks via GenericPreflight.locks/fileLockRefusals, and writable file-backed mappings as mmapFile. Current regularFiles descriptor has cursor policy union including append-only-end but regularFiles() always emits read-only-offset for any captured offset and access is only read-only or read-write-refused, so append-only candidates are not distinguished yet. Current socket classification only has TCP_FD matching /proc/net/tcp/tcp6 and cannot distinguish Unix pathname listeners, connected streams, socketpairs, datagram sockets, or abstract namespace sockets. Current anon-inode handling is path-string broad unknown except inotify; eventfd, epoll, fanotify, timerfd, signalfd, io_uring are not separately classified. Current generic file-lock matrix row is descriptor-injected harness evidence, while runtime preflight attempts blocked-lock probes, fdinfo lock lines, and /proc/locks scans. Existing matrix rows cover generic-writable-file-cursor-refusal, generic-file-lock-refusal, generic-mmap-file-refusal, generic-inotify-file-refusal, and generic-unsupported-resource-refusals, but not distinct append candidate, Unix socket subtype, eventfd, epoll, fanotify, timerfd/signalfd/io_uring baseline rows.

Implemented wave 2 baseline fail-closed classification for append-only candidates, Unix socket subtypes, and anon-inode subtypes without graduating new support. Added packages/cli/src/move-generic-wave2-baseline.ts to keep packages/cli/src/move-generic-resource-graph.ts below the 1000-line cap. Generic preflight now emits UNIX_FD rows from /proc/net/unix. Regular file descriptor state now distinguishes append-only-refused from read-write-refused and emits append-only-end cursor policy for append-only candidates while refusing them as appendOnlyRegularFileCursor. Resource-plan mapping now classifies anon_inode:[eventfd], anon_inode:[eventpoll], anon_inode:[timerfd], and anon_inode:[signalfd] as distinct resource kinds. Added focused tests and new matrix rows generic-append-only-file-cursor-refusal, generic-unix-socket-baseline-refusals, and generic-anon-inode-baseline-refusals. Coverage inventory/tooling includes the three new rows.
